per–action cortex labeling) OR host–computed cognition (the place /
goal coordinate codes handed to the navigator).
the BG action–selection cascade, in one line
Cortex learns (under dopamine) which direction to favour → its D1 "go" cells silence that direction's GPi output (disinhibition) → the thalamic relay for that
direction is released → it feeds the spiking decision, where evidence accumulates until an all–or–none commit burst picks the winner → that motor pool fires → the body moves.
In parallel a spiking actor–critic computes the reward–prediction error (reward − value, the value subtracted via the one slow–inhibition edge) and broadcasts dopamine to train the "go" weights.
The superior colliculus supplies a fast orienting bump, the cerebellum fine–tunes the motor command, and the hippocampus + prefrontal working memory supply place memory and goal–holding.

Substrate–wide simplifications: point neurons (no dendrites) · one–step conduction delay · Izhikevich point–neuron default (HH / AdEx available) · forward–Euler integration. Full list SH–1…SH–14 in the spec.

The hand–coded argmax read–out is RETIRED (kept only as the opt–in motor/thal oracle path, dashed). The spiking decision is the default: 6/6–seed GO, within 25% of the host floor (1.16×), 100% commit–burst.
This is an honest map of the code — accurate to the degree the biology is implemented here, including its reductions, not a textbook of neuroanatomy.
